images.title: Morning shift · quieter
images.intent: Bring the canal workers back to an ordinary morning.
images.writeup: Riverfolk maintain Ambrel's locks and canals while the scholars pass above them. This revision keeps the class contrast but gives the divers the tired, practical attention of people finishing a shift, rather than heroic expressions.
images.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Edit the supplied Morning shift painting. Preserve the two Riverfolk individuals, fin ears, neck gills, work clothing, maintenance tools, lock, connected bridge and smaller scholars crossing above. Make the workers substantially LESS DRAMATIC: replace both lifted, yearning heroic gazes and parted lips with relaxed closed mouths, lowered brows and task-directed looks. The foreground older worker looks down at the step and places a hand naturally to climb out; the younger worker looks down at the tool satchel she is lifting. Keep simple connected hands and readable grips. Reduce the hot orange cinematic rim light and overwhelming sunrise toward a softer, ordinary cool-peach dawn, while retaining convincing wet water reflections. A medium-close occupational scene, modest fatigue, no theatrical emotional performance. Don't change them into other people or redesign their species. Preserve the traditional oil/acrylic Breachline painted realism and matte skin. Use coherent broad light/shadow shapes and deliberate varied brush sizes, no waxy faces, no added pore noise or scratchy artificial texture. Keep focal faces/hands more defined; secondary background forms should be moderately LESS detailed and lower contrast than the original, simplified through quieter edges and fewer marks, not photographic lens blur, bokeh or a tunnel-focus effect. No text, labels, border, watermark, logo or signature. Output exactly one landscape PNG, 1536 x 1024.
